title: BPMN activities, extracted (folio-assistant-core)
description: Candidate terms extracted from every BPMN task and call activity: `name` as the label, its own `<documentation>` as the definition, the element id as the code. Generated by folio-assistant-core/scripts/glossary-extract.ts; not curated, and never hand-edited: a person promotes a term by authoring it in a glossary of their own.

terms.definition: The plan becomes beans, so a resumed session or a sibling agent can pick it up. The run's own bean was claimed by the Process_BeanOpen call before this step, so this step only notes the seeded plan on it; the beans themselves are written with the agent's own `beans create`, which no engine op performs. From here on, beans/ is the shared answer to 'what is done, what is next' — for humans and agents alike.

terms.prefLabel: Close the window back to its avatar
terms.definition: [x] closes the window back to its avatar. Only a person's [x] does this; a zoom-out never closes a window, or [x] and zooming become indistinguishable to the reader.

Leave the way back reachable: the collapsed window becomes a control in its own position and focus moves to it — left alone, focus lands on <body> and the keyboard position is lost. An action whose inverse is not reachable is not a toggle.

terms.prefLabel: Project a window onto the board
terms.definition: Project a window onto the board for the chosen card. A window is not the card grown large: it survives zooming out, and only [x] closes it. The frame is fixed ([x] always present, always in the same place); the kind fills in its declared controls.

terms.prefLabel: Raise the window the reader selected
terms.definition: Raise the selected window to the top. Selecting ANY part raises it, not just a title bar. Z-order is session-only by stated default: no z is written to the layout, so a raise is never a file write.

terms.prefLabel: Render every card as its avatar
terms.definition: Render every card as its avatar — the starting state. Each content kind controls its own avatar; the board decides only that nothing starts open.

Resolve the semantic-zoom threshold for each card's kind: the folio default unless the kind overrides it with a stated because. Return the source alongside the value, so a card that flipped too early can be traced to a decision or to a default.

terms.prefLabel: Swap cards below the threshold; leave open windows alone
terms.definition: Cards whose rendered width is strictly below the threshold swap to their avatar — automatic, driven by size. Open windows are left alone: semantic zoom and open/close are two mechanisms and must not be conflated.

terms.prefLabel: Write the note into the folio — with no coordinate
terms.definition: A new note: write it into the folio with no x, no y, no board and no position. A folio is complete with no board, and one note may sit on several boards, which a coordinate on the note could not express.

terms.prefLabel: Record x,y for this note on THIS board
terms.definition: Record the note's x,y in the layout layer for THIS board, naming the note by id. An existing card dragged here only gets a new position — placing is not creating, so no content is duplicated.

terms.prefLabel: Sweep positions whose note is gone
terms.definition: Remove every position in this board's layer whose note no longer exists. The sweep edits only the layer — one file, one pass — and never a note a person owns; a stale position must not keep a note alive.

terms.prefLabel: Name what will move, and where it lands
terms.definition: Before anything moves, name the content that would move — what it is, with its size and age — and where it lands. The confirmation sits in front of the move: an agent never relocates a durable artefact on its own initiative.

terms.prefLabel: Leave the content exactly where it is
terms.definition: The reader said no: nothing moves, no position is dropped, and the board is left exactly as it was. Drawn as its own end state because a destructive action whose refusal is not drawn gets performed by accident.

terms.prefLabel: Relocate the content to the trashcan
terms.definition: Relocate the confirmed content — that one thing, not the class it belongs to — to the trashcan. The folio changes first, because the folio carries what is true.

terms.prefLabel: Say what moved and where it went
terms.definition: Tell the reader what moved and where it went, so the content can be found in the trashcan rather than inferred missing from a card that disappeared.

terms.prefLabel: Drop its positions and sweep orphans
terms.definition: Only after the content has moved: drop its positions from the layout layer and sweep any position whose note is now gone. Sweeping first would make the board authoritative over the folio for one step.

terms.prefLabel: Record assets[] — local path or remote URL
terms.definition: kind / role / url-or-path / checksum / retrieved. A SIBLING of library:, never inside it: LibraryRef is regenerated from the tree, so an authored URL placed there is dropped on the next sync.

terms.prefLabel: Bind the folder to its bibliography slug
terms.definition: Bind the folder name to the document's bibliography slug, so library/<bib-slug>/ and its citation key are the same string: a citation resolves to a directory without a lookup table between them.
One standalone Dublin Core record per folder. dcterms is already this corpus's JSON-LD vocabulary, so this extends a live context rather than introducing one.

terms.prefLabel: Read glossary and abbreviations into candidate terms
terms.definition: The source's glossary and abbreviations sections become candidate terms of a folio-glossary/v1 scheme with the Tool glossary-from-source, verbatim, each with source file#line, and an acronym as the notation of the term it expands. Terms a person owns are never changed, and only a person moves a term to authored. A source with no such section skips this step with nothing written.

terms.prefLabel: Link L1 nodes into the corpus graph
terms.definition: Anything in library/ is L1 source content. A knowledge-graph reference from any artefact -- paper, L2, L3 -- resolves to it through library/.

Write manifest.jsonld for the folder: its @id, @type folio:SourceDocument, what it contains and its provenance, referencing the standalone dublin-core.jsonld as the record of truth rather than copying its fields.

Process_BeanClose: end the bean in a state that says why — complete and archive it, scrap it with its reasons and archive it, or record the blocker and hand it back. The one place resolve and archive are drawn; placed straight before the end so the engine's resolve sees nothing left but the archive step.

Process_BeanOpen: check before you create, find out whose the bean is, and claim it — or leave it alone when it is someone else's. The one place a claim is drawn; the gateway after this reads which end it reached.

content-change-review-committee.bpmn: compare staged against main, slice the change and review each slice, settle withdrawals and disputes, gate on coverage, review the impact, and either approve or request changes. The one judgement inside it is Call_Adjudication, whose `stands` / `withdrawn` this call accepts; public-comment, which calls this whole process, reaches it through here.
content-change-review-make.bpmn: scope the change, branch, edit content and logic, assess and absorb the downstream impact, and push.
content-change-review-publish.bpmn: merge on the owner's explicit confirmation, then remove the staging preview, rebuild main and watch it. An unmerged change keeps its preview.
content-change-review-stage.bpmn: build and deploy the branch to its staging preview, link it on the pull request, and watch the branch's CI. Runs once per push.
Author describes the content change in natural language. Example: "Update the immunization schedule to add a booster at 18 months."

Agent receives revision requests from the author and applies changes. Each push triggers a new staging deployment with updated SHA stamp. A revision push does not pass through Task_CommitPush, so for a rendered change the agent refreshes the before/after preview here (skill before-after-preview), and the next review round never reads a stale one.
Author provides feedback on what needs adjustment. Agent iterates on the feature branch.

Author reviews the rendered feature branch at <pages-url>/branches/<branch-slug>/ and compares against the main site. The staging banner shows the commit SHA. The agent's before/after preview (skill before-after-preview) sits beside the URLs, with its counts and status line.
Author submits the PR for formal review by the guidance review committee. The branches/ URL is the review surface.

adjudication.bpmn. When the editor and a reviewer, or two reviewers, disagree about a finding, an adjudicator settles it and records why; the review comment moves to `adjudicated` with the Decision that closed it. Permitted answers: `stands` — the finding is right and the author addresses it; `withdrawn` — the finding is wrong and the comment closes. Recorded on the comment, not branched: either way the flow goes on to the coverage check.

review-task.bpmn, once per slice, in parallel lanes by role. What kind of thing changed decides which review the slice descends into; the reviewer takes on that inner lane's role for the call only. Each reviewer gives the slice's blocks a verdict, and comments on the pull request with the `block:` tag where something needs saying.

The committee approves the change: the judgement, recorded with the evidence it rests on. Approving is not merging: a self-authored change cannot be approved through GitHub's own review (the approver may not be the PR's author), and a merge needs the owner's explicit confirmation whoever approved.

The review starts from the Change Set's RENDERED list (skill rendered-impact): every rendered file the change alters, predicted from each renderer's dependency cone and checked against the build. The reviewer opens every content page on it, not only the pages the author mentions; index files are listed but not reviewed. An input the renderer could not place is shown as not known, never as no change. Review committee opens both URLs side by side: - Main site: <pages-url>/ (current published state) - Staging: <pages-url>/branches/<branch-slug>/ The staging banner shows the commit SHA so they can verify what they are reviewing matches the PR. A changed figure, diagram or table is also pictured before and after on the review page, with the share of changed pixels in words (skill visual-diff, Tool folio-block-screenshots). Anything the staging job cannot picture (page chrome, scroll behaviour, a PDF page, an IG page) is in the agent's before/after preview (skill before-after-preview).

Every PR conversation comment that starts with `block: <label>` becomes a `review-comment/1.0.0` todo (open), idempotently, and is published with the preview as `review-comments.json`. The staging workflow runs this on every push and on every tagged comment; the coordinator owns that it has run before slicing, because the slices are cut around what reviewers have already said. This is the `ingest` transition of REVIEW_TRANSITIONS. Uses `folio-review-comments`.
Committee provides feedback. PR stays open. Author and agent iterate further.
Committee reviews the agent's impact assessment: - Were all downstream effects identified? - Are the indicator changes acceptable? - Does the logic change match the narrative intent?

`uses[]` is what a READER must have read to follow the block — never populated from the formal dependency graph. Once every changed block is covered, the committee checks the editorial dependencies of the change as a whole before judging its impact. Reading order is a property of folio content, so the step belongs to the content process, which reaches the harness's review by calling DOWN into `review-task`.

terms.prefLabel: Slice the change and assign reviewers
terms.definition: From the ChangeSet, its rendered list (skill rendered-impact: each changed rendered page is assigned like a changed block) and the heat map on the review page: cut the change into slices a reviewer can hold (usually a section, or a run of sections where the heat map clusters), and assign each slice to a review lane by what it contains — clinical content to a clinical SME, a decision table to a QC reviewer, prose to a narrative reviewer. A block that needs no review (a pure rename, say) is WAIVED here with a written reason, which is what the coverage gate counts. Re-entered from GW_Covered when coverage is incomplete: the uncovered blocks become new slices.

The reviewer who made a comment takes it back (it was a misreading, or a later slice answered it). Recorded with `folio-review-comment-move --to withdrawn`, committed to the edit-set's feature branch like every status change. This is the `withdraw` transition of REVIEW_TRANSITIONS.

terms.prefLabel: Options analysis how to absorb the impact
terms.definition: On the edge OUT of `Task_AssessImpact` and before `Task_CommitPush`, because the impact assessment is the evidence the options are weighed against. An analysis before it would compare ways of absorbing a downstream effect nobody has measured yet; one after the commit would be a rationalisation of a choice already pushed. Not between `Task_AssessImpact` and `Task_ReviewImpact`: those are in different processes with no sequence flow between them; the assessment reaches the committee through `Task_CompareBeforeAfter`. In the Agent lane, matching `upstream-version-adoption`: this step produces the options and their trade-offs, and `GW_Approved` in the committee review is where a decision is taken. On the trigger: reaching this call is not the same as running the whole of it. `Process_OptionsAnalysis` opens with `A_Frame`, whose trigger is `opening-brief`'s — irreversibility and surprise, not size — and leaving at that first activity is a correct outcome rather than a skipped step. A copy-edit exits immediately; a logic change that moves an indicator (from `Task_EditLogic`) does not.

Agent reviews downstream implications: - Will indicators need adjustment? - Will referral/follow-up for next visit be impacted? - Are translations affected (re-extract POT)? - Do Lean proofs still hold? skill: integration-watcher, translation-manager

Agent commits all changes to the feature branch and pushes. The feature-staging.yml workflow automatically deploys to branches/<branch-slug>/ and comments the URL on the PR. For a rendered change the agent also produces the before/after preview (skill before-after-preview) and links it in the PR body.
Agent creates a feature branch from main. Branch naming: feature/<short-description> Opens a PR immediately (AGENTS.md: "open the PR at the first commit").

Agent analyses the requested change: - Which content blocks are affected? - Are there downstream implications (indicators, referral logic, visit schedules)? - Will deterministic logic (CQL/DMN) need updating? skill: content-graph, integration-watcher
Agent modifies the relevant content blocks (.md files, block manifests). Validates each edit against the schema (content_validate). skill: content editing, block builders
If the content change affects decision logic, indicators, or workflows: - Update CQL expressions - Update DMN decision tables - Adjust indicator definitions skill: dak-authoring, fhir-pipeline
When the PR is merged or closed, the cleanup job removes the branches/<slug>/ directory from gh-pages so stale previews don't accumulate.

The owner says "merge it", and only then is the branch merged. Merge to main triggers: 1. the main site rebuilds with the changes; 2. the staging preview's cleanup runs; 3. the review comments committed on the feature branch land on main, as the review record.
docs-site.yml triggers on the merge commit to main, rebuilding the root of gh-pages with the accepted changes. The build SHA stamp now reflects the merged state.

Second dispatch point: the change was approved and merged, and the root of the site has been rebuilt from main. A failing main build can look like a green run from inside the repo. `note` rather than `claim`: the branch-watch bean already exists, and whether the publish SUCCEEDED is not this step's judgement (the build reports its own exit code). A bean is not closed on someone else's say-so, so the step records what it observed and leaves the verdict to the watcher.

feature-staging.yml triggers: 1. Regenerate docs (schema, skills, content-backed pages) 2. Render BPMN diagrams 3. Stamp build with commit SHA + timestamp + branch 4. Build Jekyll site with branches/ baseurl 5. Inject yellow staging banner into every HTML page A draft pull request is staged too, from its first push. A build takes about 22 minutes, and GitHub Pages about 3 to 4 more.

Bot comments or updates the staging URL on the PR. Includes commit SHA, branch name, and build log link, and the review list of rendered files the change alters (skill rendered-impact), each linked on the preview and on main, with any input the renderer could not place named as not known.

The stage job copies the built site into gh-pages under branches/<branch-slug>/, then `staging-share.ts apply` keeps only the files that differ from the live site. The preview's staging-sw.js serves every other file from the live site and puts the staging banner back on it. Other previews and the main site are left as they are.

First dispatch point for a CI watcher: the feature branch has changed and a staging build now exists to watch. The watcher is DISPATCHED BY OPENING A BEAN, not by a workflow_dispatch: this is a task/workflow initiation. A bean makes the watch durable past the session that opened it: the container is reclaimed, and what survives is the bean. Starting the watcher and recording that it is running are ONE declared step, so the two cannot disagree about whether anything is watching. It notes the watch on the bean rather than claiming it: only Process_BeanOpen claims a bean. The note is idempotent, so re-entering on a later push does not duplicate it.

Members read the preview and answer in their Blue columns, or leave them as they are when the change is right. They record the row's Disposition (Blue): Pending, Accepted, Partially accepted, Not accepted, Noted, Duplicate or Out of scope.

terms.prefLabel: Close the change set: the issue, then the sheet row
terms.definition: Closing is one step with two tools, GitHub and the review sheet. The agent closes the change set's issue on GitHub, with the merge or the reason it closed unmerged, then records Agentic status Closed (or Change merged) on the Agent tab through Record agent step (record-agent-step.bpmn). The sheet script then hides the row and strikes the whole row through ("make sure complete changeset rows are hidden so not cluttered and that text of that whole row is crossed out"). The agent never hides or strikes a row by hand, and never deletes one: reopening the issue and writing a new status shows it again. Hiding and striking are formatting only, which the review-log watcher ignores. A change set closed without a merge, at a person's request, takes this step too.

terms.prefLabel: Edit the document in the row's pull request
terms.definition: One row, one branch, one active pull request: the agent edits on the row's branch and opens its pull request, or updates it when the row comes round again. A closed pull request the committee wants back is reopened, or replaced by a new one on the same branch; earlier ones stay listed in Agentic status. Agentic status (Green) says where it is, and Staging review opens the preview's what-changed page. Before the preview is staged, the agent writes the change set's Disposition (change set) on the Agent tab: one line per feedback item, starting from the people's Blue Disposition, after an optional Overall statement; the sheet shows it in Disposition (agent) and flags any item without a disposition, or one that differs from the people's. It ends with Record agent step (record-agent-step.bpmn): the Agent tab row first, then Feedback (agent) from it, then the sheet read back, never Feedback (agent) alone.

The agent merges the row's pull request, and Agentic status says merged. The change set's Dispositions blurb, as it stands when Ready for merge is set to Yes, is the summary: it goes into the merge, and closes the change set's issue. It ends with Record agent step (record-agent-step.bpmn): the Agent tab row first, then Feedback (agent) from it, then the sheet read back, never Feedback (agent) alone.

Reads: the row (Title, Selected Sections, the Contributor Feedback columns, Disposition) and the sections it names. Writes: a proposed direction in Feedback (agent) (Green), and the row's feedback basis on the Agent tab, so the script can tell when the feedback has moved on. A question for people goes in Feedback (agent) as a Decision needed block with options and a recommendation, and the row's Agentic status becomes Needs human; a chat card may repeat it, but the sheet is the record. An answered question leaves the feedback: its decision is added to the change set's Disposition (change set) on the Agent tab, shown in Disposition (agent), whose decision history is appended to and never removed. It ends with Record agent step (record-agent-step.bpmn): the Agent tab row first, then Feedback (agent) from it, then the sheet read back, never Feedback (agent) alone.

terms.prefLabel: QA gate: review dispositions against the people and the pull request
terms.definition: Reads: the change set's Disposition (change set), the people's Blue Disposition and feedback, the pull request's diff at its head commit, and the staging QA report. Checks that every feedback item has one disposition; that each agrees with the people's Blue Disposition; that each Accepted or Partially accepted item has the change in the diff, and a Not accepted, Noted, Duplicate or Out of scope item has none; that the diff changes nothing no disposition accounts for; and that the QA report for the staged commit has no failing gate. Writes: QA gate (change set) on the Agent tab, first line "Passed <head sha>: …" or "Failed <head sha>: <why>", and QA report (change set), the report's link. The sheet shows the gate under Staging review; a pass for an older commit reads as stale. It ends with Record agent step (record-agent-step.bpmn): the Agent tab row first, then Feedback (agent) from it, then the sheet read back, never Feedback (agent) alone.

terms.prefLabel: Set Ready for agent to Yes
terms.definition: An Editor agrees the direction and sets the row's Ready for agent (Orange) to Yes. Person-only: the agent never sets it.

terms.prefLabel: Set Ready for merge to Yes
terms.definition: An Editor sets the row's Ready for merge (Orange) to Yes once the QA gate has passed for the pull request's head commit. Person-only. Set earlier, the agent does not merge until the gate passes, and its feedback says so.

A member adds a row on the Contributor Feedback tab: a title, the Selected Sections it is about (a dropdown from the document's table of contents) and their feedback in their own Blue column. The script gives the row its Change-set id and links each section.

terms.prefLabel: Filter the corpus, choose the granularity, decompose the question
terms.definition: The paper's Planner. Three outputs, and the middle one is the method's substance: a filtered document subset, the granularity to search at, and the sub-questions. CHOOSING THE GRANULARITY PER QUESTION is the whole point of parsing at several. A broad question is answered from summaries and a specific one from chunks; a pipeline that picks once has answered every future question the same way. This checkout cannot yet offer the choice — `l1-blocks.ts` produces blocks, there is no summary level — so this step SAYS which granularity it searched rather than implying the corpus offered alternatives. Re-entered on every iteration, not only the first: the sub-questions are re-derived from what has been found so far, which is what makes the loop a search rather than a retry.

terms.prefLabel: Deduplicate, and keep what is actually relevant
terms.definition: The paper's Refiner. Accumulates into the evidence set the report is built from — so what is dropped here is invisible downstream, which is why it is a step somebody performs rather than a filter buried in retrieval.

terms.prefLabel: Synthesise, cite to a location, and say what was not found
terms.definition: The paper's Reporter, with two obligations it does not state. CITE TO A LOCATION, not to a document — the page and bounding box the parse preserved, so a reader verifies a claim where it was made rather than being sent to a PDF. AND SAY WHAT WAS NOT FOUND. The failure this method makes easy is that a search which ended quietly looks exactly like one that succeeded. Sub-questions that returned nothing are reported, distinguishing "not in the corpus" from "not found by this search" — only the first is a fact about the folio. A figure description an agent drafted is NOT reported as what the figure shows. `schemas/narrative.ts` holds that line and this step does not cross it.

The paper's Searcher, at the granularity A_Plan chose. Which retrieval paradigm — text-only, vision-only or hybrid — is recorded in the methodology node as an open trade-off rather than settled here: the paper's comparison was measured on its own corpus and says nothing about a folio's.
NOT IMPLEMENTED; see docs/document-ingestion.md. Tar/zip is opaque to every grep in the corpus until its contents are listed as data.
No Tool yet; the method, and the choice of recogniser, is skill audio-transcription.
NOT IMPLEMENTED; see docs/document-ingestion.md. Applies equally to an image EXTRACTED FROM A PDF, not only to an uploaded one.

terms.prefLabel: Cite the author of every narrative
terms.definition: A generated description is a claim by someone. Record whether a human or an agent wrote it, and for an agent the model version. An uncited narrative is indistinguishable from a transcription of the source.
Tools tabular-csv and tabular-xlsx, as CSVW (skill tabular-metadata). CSV and spreadsheet: tabs, column and row headers, sizes, and what the dataset is about.

terms.prefLabel: File info, sizes, hashes, timestamps, mimetype
terms.definition: NOT IMPLEMENTED; see docs/document-ingestion.md. Mechanical and cheap; the checksum is what makes a remote asset verifiable.

The document draws on library sources; every statement extracted from them is published in the document's own pages and in the shared extraction viewer, each linked to its library entry and section, before the document is rendered. The same sub-process ingestion calls when an entry is promoted: here it catches a source the document took up since, and a statement changed since. How the pages look is this content type's, through its adapter.
Core's shared review-and-publish process (Process_FolioReviewPublish): the reviewer reads the rendered folio and approves it, asks for changes, or sends a working draft to the Authoring Committee.

Every block edit runs the HCI validation gate — see editing-hci-validation.bpmn. A normative statement is a `recommendation` block, drafted through normative-statements: one statement per block, a folio-chosen label, and its strength as a code in a declared code list, so a reviewer signs off each one individually.
Scope it: chapters, the blocks each needs, which statements are normative.
content_profile_check: no math kind, no lean field, no .lean sibling. A paper folio has no such step; this is why a document folio needs neither Lean nor TeX to publish.
Assemble to Markdown, then pandoc. The PDF goes through an HTML engine — never latexmk.
folio_init writes content/, uploads/, library/, the manifests, the builder shim and AGENTS.md. Skipped when the folio already exists.
