Comments on the frozen, line-numbered review version of the public template are placed, triaged, weighed and decided (public-comment.bpmn). Private annexes are never circulated.

The parties agree the purpose, the datasets, the period, the conditions and duties, which trust anchors each side accepts, and the legal basis the sharing rests on (consent, treatment, public-health law or a research waiver). This sets what the text must say; it is a negotiation between people.

terms.prefLabel: P2.1 · Assign version and fixed URL
terms.definition: Each signed version gets its own immutable URL (for example /dsa/42/v3). A 'latest' URL may exist; nothing cites it. A new version never overwrites an old one. This fixed-version URL is the one a Consent cites (consent rule 2), and a computable agreement's ODRL policy uid is set to it (P2.3).

One DCAT 3 record: the agreement as a catalogued resource, each file a dcat:Distribution with dcat:downloadURL and spdx:checksum; datasets it covers carry odrl:hasPolicy. Versions are linked with DCAT 3 versioning (previous version, version, current version).

terms.prefLabel: P1.4 · Check the ODRL against the text
terms.definition: Computable only. A person checks that the ODRL says what the text says, and signs it off. A program can check the ODRL is well formed; it cannot check that it matches the text. The check includes the consent duty: present when the legal basis is consent, absent otherwise (consent rule 1).

terms.prefLabel: P2.2b · State the URL and hash to cite
terms.definition: Consent-based only. The version's publication metadata states the fixed-version URL (P2.1) and the hash (P2.2) that a Consent cites in FHIR R4 Consent.policy.uri (consent rule 2), never the 'latest' URL. For a computable agreement that URL is also the ODRL policy uid (P2.3): a Consent counts only when its Consent.policy.uri equals the agreement's ODRL policy uid, so the two are the same string.
The parties decide what happens to the agreement. Deciding to amend or terminate is human; expiry of a computable agreement is already enforced by its ODRL dateTime constraint.

terms.prefLabel: P14.2 · Decide what happens to existing grants
terms.definition: Existing grants keep citing the old hash. The parties decide, per agreement: they stay valid until expiry, or they are revoked and reissued against the new version (in smart-trust). The old version stays readable.

Computable only. One assigner and one assignee (ODRL 2.2 §2.1.3), permissions and prohibitions with target assets (§2.2), constraints (§2.5.1) and duties (§2.6.3), written as JSON-LD. Purposes from HL7 PurposeOfUse. Consent rule 1: the Agreement carries the odrl:obtainConsent duty only when the legal basis recorded in P1.2a is consent.

terms.prefLabel: Revoke grants and start end-of-agreement duties
terms.definition: All grants are revoked (P13) and the end-of-agreement duties start: return or delete the data, then check them (P12). Those are server processes in smart-trust; this step records that the parties started them.
Compute SHA-256 (FIPS 180-4) of the signed text, and of the ODRL file if there is one, recorded as DCAT 3 spdx:checksum and verified by check:dsa-hash.

Consent-based only. Record the SHA-256 of the plain-language summary beside the agreement's, in the same version (consent rule 3). The summary a person consented to can then be checked against the agreement it summarises; a changed summary is a new version.

The amendment widens use, so a Consent citing the old version's URL and hash does not cover the new version (consent rule 2). Record on the bean, and in the new version's text, that new consent is needed; the new version gets its own plain-language summary (P1.2b). Asking each person again is the trust layer's.

terms.prefLabel: P2.3 · Make the ODRL cite the text
terms.definition: The ODRL policy names the signed text distribution with dcterms:source (DCMI Terms), pointing at the immutable URL whose spdx:checksum was just recorded. Its uid is that same fixed-version URL, the URL a Consent cites in Consent.policy.uri (consent rule 2).

Consent-based only. Write a plain-language summary of the agreement in the same document folio: what it lets the recipient do with the person's data, in words the person can read. Consent rule 3: every agreement that needs consent publishes this summary, hashed with the agreement (P2.2a), and the summary is what the person consents to. It is reviewed, rendered and versioned with the text.

terms.prefLabel: Publish the version at its URL
terms.definition: Publish the files at the version's immutable URL. If the parties' names are sensitive, publish only the template and the hash of the signed instance. A consent-based agreement publishes its plain-language summary and its hash with the text (consent rule 3). Check before publishing (consent rule 2): a computable agreement's ODRL policy uid equals this version's fixed-version URL, the URL a Consent cites; if they differ, the version is not published.

The text states the legal basis the parties agreed in P1.1 as a normative statement: consent, treatment, public-health law, or a research waiver. Consent rule 1: only an agreement whose legal basis is consent carries the odrl:obtainConsent duty; treatment, public-health law and research waivers do not rest on consent. The gateway that follows, the ODRL and the reviewers all read the basis from this statement.

terms.prefLabel: Render the text to HTML and PDF
terms.definition: Render the agreed text to the form that will be signed (HTML and PDF), without a TeX installation. A consent-based agreement's plain-language summary is rendered with it.

Legal and policy review of the whole draft. Reviewers comment on blocks through review-comments; review says which review skill answers which question. For a consent-based agreement the reviewers also check that the plain-language summary says what the text says, since it is what the person consents to (consent rule 3).

terms.prefLabel: P14.5 · Set the status to ended
terms.definition: Set the life-cycle status of the agreement's DCAT 3 record (DCAT 3 §6.4.30). The published versions stay readable at their URLs.
The signatories sign: wet ink, or an electronic signature under national law. Technically a detached JWS (RFC 7515) or CMS (RFC 5652); PAdES for a signed PDF needs the owner's approval.

terms.prefLabel: P1.5 · Split public terms from private annexes
terms.definition: Split the agreement into a public template and private annexes (security controls, named staff). Only the hash of a private annex is ever published.

Write the agreement as a document folio: one normative statement per clause the parties must keep, through normative-statements. The text says which governs if it and a machine-readable form disagree (suggested: the text).

On the edge out of `Task_ReviewFindings` and before `Task_RecordDecision`: the findings are the evidence, so the options can only be weighed once they exist, and after `Task_RecordDecision` the decision is already written down. Not between `Gateway_EditorDecision` and `Task_RecordDecision`: `Flow_21b` runs `Task_RecordDecision` -> `Gateway_EditorDecision`, so the gateway reads a decision already recorded. In the Agent lane: the subprocess records that the options were WEIGHED (its own `decision-audit` note), and `Task_RecordDecision` in `Lane_Editor` records WHAT WAS CHOSEN. The analyst is not the decider. (`CallActivity_Evidence` is in `Lane_Editor` because the author performs the retrieval.) On the trigger: `A_Frame` opens the subprocess on `opening-brief`'s trigger — irreversibility and surprise — and leaving there is a correct outcome. A spelling fix that reached `Task_ReviewFindings` with one mechanical finding exits immediately; a revise-or-discard on a block other content depends on does not.

Before anything is drafted: the author reads the guidance ALREADY in this content, frames the question as PICO, retrieves candidates across the three evidence classes, and has each candidate's authority resolved against its publisher's own API. A recommendation reaches the drafting step with its evidence attached, or with the gap recorded. This step has nothing to do for content that carries no recommendations -- a mathematics folio has none, and a figure redrawn from its own source adds none -- and the subprocess's first gateway (Gateway_RecommendationInPlay) ends it there at its own event, recording the answer, rather than satisfying the search vacuously.
A review agent judges what no checker can: accuracy, voice, exposition, whether the change says what the editor meant.
Lean build and proof status, LaTeX compile, FHIR/SUSHI validation, QA axes.

Process_BeanOpen: check before you create, find out whose the bean is, and claim it — or leave it alone when it is someone else's. The one place a claim is drawn; the gateway after this reads which end it reached.
Mechanical results and review findings are merged into one report against the proposed change.
Only now does the change become corpus content, together with its QA sidecars. Subject to the commit-hygiene requirement.
The editor states the change in natural language; no content has moved yet.

The authoring agent produces a PROPOSED change. Nothing is written to the corpus yet. For a rendered change it also produces the before/after preview (skill before-after-preview) here, before Gateway_ValidationFork, so the preview exists when the parallel review starts.
Findings are appended to the bean, so the next agent or human sees what is outstanding.

terms.prefLabel: Record the decision and audit note
terms.definition: A decision is an act ABOUT the findings, not a finding. Record the outcome, every finding it weighed, every finding it overrules — and an audit note saying why it was made, or why a finding in it was left. Each note cites corpus evidence: a witness, another finding, a QA report, a block, a file range. An overruled mechanical finding stays on the record; a gate whose findings vanish when somebody disagrees with them cannot be audited. An agent may assemble the citations and is recorded as `proposed_by`; the author is whoever decided.

Process_BeanClose: end the bean in a state that says why — complete and archive it, scrap it with its reasons and archive it, or record the blocker and hand it back. The one place resolve and archive are drawn; placed straight before the end so the engine's resolve sees nothing left but the archive step.
THE GATE: the editor sees every finding BEFORE anything reaches the corpus.

The editor chose revise: rework the proposed change against the findings the editor reviewed, then send it back through validation as a new proposal. The before/after preview is refreshed with it (skill before-after-preview).
Block schema, label prefixes, required fields, constraint rules.

Escalated to a human reviewer or subject-matter expert when the change turns on clinical or scientific judgement. A rendered change reaches the reviewer with its before/after preview (skill before-after-preview).
Syntax, spelling, cross-references, citation and link resolution.

terms.prefLabel: Appraise and grade the body of evidence
terms.definition: Certainty of evidence per the grading system the folio declares. The grade attaches to the BODY of evidence for one PICO question, not to an individual citation -- which is why this step is after the join and not inside the fan-out.

The PICO, the graded body of evidence, each verified citation and its resolved authority record are written onto the recommendation block, so a reader can retrace the whole chain from the sentence back to the source.

terms.prefLabel: Query data repositories and statistical datasets
terms.definition: Indicator and microdata sources. Distinct from the two above because the unit of evidence is a MEASUREMENT with a population, a period and a method, not a claim in prose.

Population, Intervention, Comparator, Outcome. The PICO is what makes the search reproducible and the evidence auditable: without it, 'we looked for evidence' is not a claim anyone can check. WHO guideline development states the question this way before any retrieval.

Ingested primary literature under library/: the sections/*.md tree and, where a document was scanned, ocr/page-NNN.txt. NOTE the known blind spot — a document OCR'd but never re-run through pdf-structure.py has only a stub in sections/, so a sections-only search misses it.

terms.prefLabel: Search trusted L2 and L3 content
terms.definition: Already-adjudicated guidance: WHO SMART DAKs at L2 and FHIR Implementation Guides at L3. A recommendation adopted in a published DAK is evidence of a different kind from a primary study -- it is a prior decision, with its own provenance, and must be cited as that rather than laundered into primary evidence. NOT YET SKILL-BACKED: no skill searches adjudicated L2/L3 content for evidence. `corpus-grep` is a different task (checking that a gap is really open).

Insufficient evidence is a RESULT. It is recorded as such -- an honest gap the guideline can state -- rather than being closed by weakening the recommendation until the available evidence supports it.

terms.prefLabel: Open a bean for the unverified citation
terms.definition: An unresolvable citation is not dropped and not silently kept. It becomes a tracked item, so the gap is visible in the work plan rather than surviving as a footnote nobody re-checks.

The author reads what the document, DAK or IG ALREADY says on this question, before looking outward. A recommendation that contradicts a sibling recommendation in the same artefact is a defect no external evidence will reveal.

Each candidate is resolved against the standard API of the body that publishes it, so that 'authoritative' is a RESOLVED FACT rather than an assertion in the citation. What is checked: that the identifier resolves at the publisher; that the retrieved record matches what the citation claims; that the version and date are the ones cited; and that the publisher is one this folio has declared trusted. STRAWPERSON: the concrete registry list and endpoints are not settled here -- see the cat-harness.processes:policy note.
candidates.json holds extracted theorems and definitions. Proposals only -- never adjudicated verdicts.

The document has a text layer: extract it with pdf-extract (pdfminer.six, then a zero-dependency content-stream reader). Exit 2 means no text layer — a scan — and routes to OCR; it is not an empty document.

A document ingested this way keeps its text in ocr/ and only a stub in sections/, which the documented sections/ grep cannot see. That asymmetry is why the corpus-grep checklist has a fourth tier. The run also records WHICH SOFTWARE made the pages, in ocr/run-context.json: a folio-run-context/v1 (cat-harness schemas/run-context.ts, the record test runs and QA reports use for the same question), naming the OCR engine, the rasteriser and each language model with its version and the sha256 of the bytes that ran. Two OCRs of one scan can read differently ("Manual" and "Manval"), and without it neither could be told from the other or reproduced.

terms.prefLabel: Split into sections/*.md with doc_brief front-matter
terms.definition: Contextual retrieval: a chunk in isolation loses what makes it mean anything, so each section carries the document brief.

Write structure.json (pdf-structure/v1): doc id, TOC from the PDF outline or inferred from headings, page ranges, metadata, and source{} with the sha256 and a mimetype sniffed from the bytes, never the extension. A structure that could not be determined says so in structure_note rather than being rendered as one. For OCR'd text, source.runContext cites the OCR step's run context by sha256. A title already known for the document (the catalogue's dc.title, or one given with --title) is passed through as the raw title, so the sections' doc_title does not carry a scan's misreading.

Process_ContributorFeedback: while the document is a working draft, the Authoring Committee gives feedback through the Contributor Feedback sheet, and each change set is edited and merged in its own pull request. When its changes are merged, the document is validated and rendered again.
See draft-to-publication.bpmn for the review and release path this expands into. Release authorisation is not relaxable.

The reviewer this folio binds. authoring-document relaxes the base SME step precisely because no single lane fits every document. Review the rendered folio, not a description of it, and record the feedback. The outcome is iterate — back to authoring — or approved for the publication path.

Process_BeanClose: end the bean in a state that says why — complete and archive it, scrap it with its reasons and archive it, or record the blocker and hand it back. The one place resolve and archive are drawn; placed straight before the end so the engine's resolve sees nothing left but the archive step.

Process_BeanOpen: check before you create, find out whose the bean is, and claim it — or leave it alone when it is someone else's. The one place a claim is drawn; the gateway after this reads which end it reached.

The question is presented as a short list of selectable options, never as free prose, and the list names the top-level content types the agent knows about. The answer becomes the statedIntent fact and the table is evaluated again — the user's answer is read as evidence, like any other fact.

A PERSON'S STEP: the scan's `markers` that are not yet declared are offered as selectable options — one per marker, each with its paths and what declaring it means, plus "none of these" — and the person picks which parts of the repository to load into the KG. A tap card where the host has one; otherwise a numbered pick-list with a stated default. Never a typed reply. The default declares NOTHING. Only the picks reach Task_Scaffold, which declares exactly those in index.config.json. With no undeclared marker found, nothing is asked. The same question is put after setup by running the scan with `--markers` (repo-conversion §2a).

terms.prefLabel: Import what, where, and who does it
terms.definition: Three questions the scan cannot answer: import these or not; library or content for each group; leave the files where they are or reorganize to declutter. Plus whether to dispatch one ingestion agent or a small swarm. Non-relaxable: nobody's files are moved or imported on inference.
Only on the new-repo branch, and only after the user has named it. An empty working directory is scaffolded in place instead.

Before the first question is asked, establish HOW to ask it: audio, ordinary chat, selectable options for a user with limited hand function, large-type for low vision. A user who finds the questions unusable never reaches the rest of this diagram.

terms.prefLabel: Start the Pages build and derive the URL
terms.definition: scripts/pages-bootstrap.ts: check the gh-pages branch first (absent is `unprovisioned`), derive the site URL from the git remote or the instance's config (its index.config.json entry), report whether a publish workflow exists and the Pages source it needs, and optionally probe until the site answers.

Before Pages is switched on, make sure the gh-pages branch exists — the semantics of A_Provision in bootstrap-tools' render-kg-to-github-pages.bpmn, first half. `git ls-remote --heads origin gh-pages`; if absent, `bun run cat-harness/scripts/pages-bootstrap.ts --provision` pushes an orphan gh-pages holding a placeholder index.html and .nojekyll (idempotent; never forced; the script creates no remote branch without the flag). Then Settings → Pages → "Deploy from a branch: gh-pages, / (root)" — not "GitHub Actions" when the publish workflow pushes gh-pages. Every publishing path reaches this step: new-repo, overlay and add-folio, and an overlay or new repo that remote-mounts its dependencies.

Mechanical, read-only: does the instance's config (its `index.config.json` entry; a legacy `<name>.config.json` only as a fallback) declare a contentType, does the working tree hold somebody's existing project, and what has the user actually said. These are the three inputs to folio-intent.dmn. Non-relaxable: scaffolding without looking first is how a folio gets written over somebody's project.
A measured 404. The author is told the address and that the first build has not landed there yet.

terms.prefLabel: Say it could not be confirmed
terms.definition: No URL, no probe, or a failed request. Reported as "could not check", never as "not yet" and never as "live".
Confirmed live. The link is given as a link, and the author is told what is on it.

content/, uploads/, library/, the first manifests, <slug>.json and index.config.json (the instance's config inline in its entry; no <slug>.config.json), the builder shim, AGENTS.md with its stubs, .mcp.json, the session-start hook and the beans store. On the overlay path it declares in index.config.json exactly the markers picked at Task_ChooseHarnessed, and none it was not given. Refuses rather than overwrites when a folio is already present.

terms.prefLabel: Scan the repo for content worth importing
terms.definition: Read-only. Classifies candidates into library/ (external source) and content/ (authored here), and reports what it could not classify as its own bucket rather than forcing every file into one of the two. Its fourth section, `markers`, lists the content markers it found — sushi-config.yaml, a legacy dak.json, .bpmn processes, a beans store, library/, Lean, folio manifests — each with its paths, whether index.config.json already declares it (declared, not-declared, or unknown), and the snippet that would. `bun run cat-harness-tools/scripts/scan-repo-content.ts --json`, a plain command any agent host can run.
The first beans: what the author said they want to get started on, one bean per top-level content object they named.

terms.prefLabel: Publish the version with its change notes
terms.definition: The publisher states what changed, what was added and what was withdrawn, and why, in words a country team can act on. The notes go with the release, so the comparison below starts from the publisher's own account rather than only from a diff.

terms.prefLabel: Decide each adaptation: keep, revise or retire
terms.definition: One recorded decision per affected adaptation, with its reason: keep it as is, revise it to the new version, or retire it because the new version now covers it. A decision to diverge from the new version is recorded as such.

terms.prefLabel: Compare old, new and our adaptations
terms.definition: Attach the impact report to the re-pin: the changes that reach this site (only what it mounts), and its own files that look like adaptations of a changed file. The team adds what a diff cannot see: which policies, local decisions and translations rest on the changed text.

terms.prefLabel: Map the affected layers in order
terms.definition: Run the re-pin planner (mount:repin:cone) with the fleet and the changed repository. It lists every site downstream in waves, so a site moves only after the layers it takes from have moved, and marks which sites are ready now.

terms.prefLabel: Merge the re-pin with its decided revisions
terms.definition: The re-pin merges when its checks are green and every decision it needs is recorded. Its pull request cites the decisions, which become the release notes for this site's update.

terms.prefLabel: Open the re-pin for the next ready layer
terms.definition: For each site that is ready now, open one re-pin pull request that moves its pins from the old version to the new one. Its staging preview is a full build with QA. A site's standing consent may let its own workflow open this pull request.
The committee reads the old version, the new version and each affected adaptation side by side on the staging preview, and hears the adaptation team's account of what rests on them.
Each revision is an ordinary content change, reviewed on its staging preview through content change review, on the re-pin's branch or a branch that merges with it.

Process_BeanClose: end the bean in a state that says why — complete and archive it, scrap it with its reasons and archive it, or record the blocker and hand it back. The one place resolve and archive are drawn; placed straight before the end so the engine's resolve sees nothing left but the archive step.

Process_BeanOpen: check before you create, find out whose the bean is, and claim it — or leave it alone when it is someone else's. The one place a claim is drawn; the gateway after this reads which end it reached.

The harness's `document-ingestion.bpmn`: accept the upload by a declared route, extract its metadata into the KG, and catalogue the asset in library/ — placed if materialized, recorded as referenced if not. Everything below refines that result for a document. Called, not copied.
See ingest-build-l1-kg.bpmn.
See ingest-derive-content.bpmn. Most of this subprocess is not implemented yet.
See ingest-extract-structure.bpmn.

See ingest-l1-completeness-gate.bpmn. Skill-backed by `l1-document-ingestion`: its section "What a complete L1 entry holds" names `check:l1-complete` as the gate and states its three results. The gate contains one adjudication (Task_FlagDrift: `real`, `spurious` or `source-wrong`), and its own Task_Verdict records the answer as a reason against the verdict before returning. So both answers reach this step, and nothing here branches on them; Gateway_Complete branches on the gate's completeness verdict instead.
See ingest-theme.bpmn. The subprocess derives one Theme node with kind sticky|webpage|publication, and refuses a source it cannot complete rather than emitting a partial theme.

terms.prefLabel: Publish the extracted statements with source links
terms.definition: THE ENTRY IS COMPLETE HERE, so its statements are published here. Every statement the extraction captured from this entry (a recommendation, a requirement, a candidate a person still has to rule on) becomes readable in two places: the folio's working artifact, in the pages its content profile renders, and the shared extraction viewer. Each one links back to the library entry and to the section it came from. WHY IN INGESTION AND NOT LATER. A statement nobody can read beside its source is reviewed from memory, or not at all. Publishing when the entry is promoted means a reviewer can check every extracted statement against its source the moment it exists. The sub-process is the same for every content type. The content type decides only how its pages look, through its adapter. An entry that yields no statements (a referenced source, a dataset) passes through it with nothing to publish, and says so.

terms.prefLabel: Available to cite as an L1 source
terms.definition: Every knowledge-graph reference to this source now resolves through library/. Authoring and review consume it from here -- see authoring-a-document.bpmn.

terms.prefLabel: Detect media type, mint a doc id
terms.definition: Sniff the media type rather than trusting the extension, and mint the doc id from the page-1 arXiv stamp where there is one, else from the filename.

terms.prefLabel: Establish the licence from the upload
terms.definition: EARLY: before any derivation, because library/ is holds: content and anything derived first is committed, so refusing it later is a deletion nobody may take unasked. This step sees only the upload itself — the licence recorded in its intake.json (the same stated / unknown record a library manifest carries) and whether a LICENSE file sits beside it. It never infers a licence from extracted text. The verdict is stated, unknown, or UNDETERMINED, and undetermined is never reported as cleared: the pipeline proceeds and says so, because a licence that only extraction can reveal is a later check's to find.

terms.prefLabel: Record the gap as a bean
terms.definition: A missing derived artefact is a tracked gap, not a silent omission. The document stays in uploads/ until the gap closes.
The folder name IS the bibliography citation key, so a citation and a directory are the same string.

A QA sidecar of general document ingestion, drained slowly. Nothing is written to ENQUEUE a block: the queue is derived (every prose block in every declared library, minus those whose summaries.json record is a current draft or confirmation), so a promoted entry is in it the moment its blocks are. A re-ingested document whose text changed re-enters it on its own, because the record's source_hash no longer matches. What an agent doing ingestion work does here is DRAIN a few: `bun run cat summaries:next -- --n K` hands it the next K blocks with their text, it writes a short summary of each in its own words, and `bun run cat summaries:record` writes them into library/<bib-slug>/summaries.json as drafts naming the agent and its model. The block itself stays verbatim and `ingested`. ADVISORY, never a gate: this step does not hold up Task_Citeable, and check:l1-complete reports the backlog (`block-summaries`) without failing on it. Confirming or rejecting a draft is a person's act, in `bun run cat narratives`.
L1 source to L1 KG is NOT complete while a required derived artefact is missing. This is the gate that makes the derivation steps obligatory rather than aspirational.
A machine can detect that two readings differ. Which one is right is a human call.

Back-translate each localized narrative into its source language and compare the meaning, to catch semantic drift and bad terminology that a forward-only check cannot see. Agentic. Two parties are kept apart under untainted-verification: a back-translator that sees ONLY the target-language text, and an adjudicator that sees the original and the back-translation and rules. The verdict is recorded per block, under criterion `translation-semantic-roundtrip` in the block's `<block>.<locale>.translation-qa.json` sidecar, by the `translation-roundtrip-record` Tool (translation-manager §5). A terminology miss is a different criterion, `translation-terms-preserved` (acronyms, numbers, URLs that must survive), so Gateway_Drift can tell the two apart. Never close this step by reversing the PO's msgid→msgstr map: that returns the source exactly and scores 1.0 always. An empty `translation-semantic-roundtrip` entry list means "not yet run", which is never a pass.

Record the completeness verdict in three states — met, unmet, or not yet derivable — as bun run cat check:l1-complete reports it. Not-yet-derivable is never a pass. An unmet verdict opens a bean and returns to derivation; only a met one lets the entry into library/.

Process_BeanClose: end the bean in a state that says why — complete and archive it, scrap it with its reasons and archive it, or record the blocker and hand it back. The one place resolve and archive are drawn; placed straight before the end so the engine's resolve sees nothing left but the archive step.

Process_BeanOpen: check before you create, find out whose the bean is, and claim it — or leave it alone when it is someone else's. The one place a claim is drawn; the gateway after this reads which end it reached.
See editing-hci-validation.bpmn. Runs once per proposed change, not once per cycle.
See draft-to-publication.bpmn.
Implementer and reader feedback on the published folio, triaged by severity and scope.
Triaged feedback re-enters the work plan as beans, which is how the next cycle knows what it is for.
Scope the work, identify artifacts and actors, form the team, set the timeline.

No more content is planned: deprecate the folio. Post a deprecation notice and timeline, update its status metadata, archive it, point references at any successor, and remove it from active publication. The programme manager decides; retirement archives rather than deletes.

The plan becomes beans, so a resumed session or a sibling agent can pick it up. The run's own bean was claimed by the Process_BeanOpen call before this step, so this step only notes the seeded plan on it; the beans themselves are written with the agent's own `beans create`, which no engine op performs. From here on, beans/ is the shared answer to 'what is done, what is next' — for humans and agents alike.
Corpus-wide checks that a single-block gate cannot make: cross-references, build green, proof status, QA axes across the whole folio.
The editing sub-process. Every change to the corpus goes through its HCI validation gate — a red draft is fixed there, never by patching the built artifact.

When the draft goes out for public comment: the release date is agreed, the draft is frozen as a line-numbered public comment release, every channel is set up against it and announced, and the comments that come back are placed, triaged, recommended on by the review committee and decided by the editor (Process_PublicCommentRelease, which calls Process_PublicComment).

Process_BeanClose: end the bean in a state that says why — complete and archive it, scrap it with its reasons and archive it, or record the blocker and hand it back. The one place resolve and archive are drawn; placed straight before the end so the engine's resolve sees nothing left but the archive step.
Publication requires authorisation by the programme manager or designated authority.
Render the corpus into the draft form of the folio: PDF, HTML site, or FHIR IG.
The draft publication is circulated to the review team for formal review.
What shipped is resolved; what slipped stays open and carries into the next cycle.

terms.prefLabel: Open beans for the change requests
terms.definition: Each requested change becomes a bean, so the editors and agents picking the work up next see exactly what review asked for and what is still open.

Process_BeanOpen: check before you create, find out whose the bean is, and claim it — or leave it alone when it is someone else's. The one place a claim is drawn; the gateway after this reads which end it reached.
Publication-readiness QA across layers — QC reports, IG Publisher QA, proof status, broken links, build warnings.

Version bump, release notes, tag, build the final artifacts, deploy to the publication platform. The deploy is the general render-kg-to-cdn step with the RELEASE root as its publication root URL — the same step a staging preview takes with a root under it; the target (GitHub Pages, or a folio's own platform) is chosen by its Tool.
Content reviewer, QC reviewer and technical officer review the draft as a whole — coherence, phase-gate criteria, breaking vs non-breaking change.
Domain sign-off: clinical SMEs for a guideline, subject-matter reviewers for a paper.

terms.prefLabel: Make the change, check it and merge it
terms.definition: The second phase, drawn on its own page (public-comment-change.bpmn): an author edits the document as decided on a feature branch, the change set is reviewed on its staging preview, an independent QA gate checks the dispositions against the pull request, and each comment it answers is marked incorporated when it merges. A withdrawal still interrupts the comment while this runs.
public-comment assign: by GitHub login. A committee member who recommends on an unassigned comment is assigned it as they do.

terms.prefLabel: Recommend a decision, with a rationale
terms.definition: A GitHub comment tagged pc: PC-0042 / recommend: code, from a login in config.json committee, or public-comment recommend.

public-comment decide, or decide: code on GitHub from a login in config.json editors. accepted, accepted-modified, not-accepted, noted, deferred; a reason for all but accepted. Also reopens a decided comment.

terms.prefLabel: Agree each change-set's requirements on its issue
terms.definition: A change-set gets its primary GitHub issue the first time somebody engages with it (the Discuss form, a recommendation or decision on one of its comments, a mention, a PR), opened by the folio's public-comment workflow; any number of other issues may discuss it and are linked. People agree the requirements there, and the committee or editor changes the record with cs-add / cs-remove / cs-title / cs-requirements / cs-committee / cs-merge / cs-split / cs-close / cs-new. Making change-sets is people's, in any of three ways, each like opening an issue: a row on the review sheet's Review Change Sets with only a Title (the sheet script gives it the next id), a change-set issue from the folio's change-set issue form, or feedback that says a change-set should be split, merged or moved. For the last two the agent proposes the change-sets and which comments go where, as a Decision needed question, and makes them only once an Editor sets Ready for agent to Yes. A comment is moved by typing another change-set's id, or new, in Change Set (human). The issue's change-set section is rendered from the record and put back if hand-edited; the nightly reconcile keeps every issue in line. The issue is for requirements; the PR that closes it is for preview, review and approval.

public-comment import / import-narrative: one record per row or cited passage, anchored through review-anchors.json. Status: received. When the review is also kept in a shared Google Sheet, build its Apps Script with Tool review-sheet-sync (from review/public-comment/sheet-sync.json) and have the sheet's owner install it once (Extensions, Apps Script, run installTriggers): the sheet then keeps its page, section, line and comment links and its change-set joins current by itself.

terms.prefLabel: Propose change-sets, as records with no issue yet
terms.definition: public-comment-changesets seed / propose: the agent groups the comments to be weighed into change-sets, one per change the document may need, each a record under changesets/ with its requirements and members. A PROPOSAL: nothing is decided, no GitHub issue is opened, and a comment may sit in zero, one or several change-sets. The record is the only one; everything shown about a change-set is rendered from it. A comment that arrives later is triaged the same way (Tool review-log-watch, cs-requests.ts triage): the agent suggests an open change-set that shares its sections, or a new one, and the committees (TWG) of that change-set, as its own suggestion only; a person's Change Set (human) or TWG (human) on the review sheet always wins. How a change-set came about does not matter: people adjudicate it.

public-comment-changesets reroute, or cs-committee: <TWG> — <why> on GitHub from a person in the committee or editor lane. Moves the change-set to another TWG review committee and records who, when, from, to and why on the change-set record, so re-ingesting comments never resets it. Person-only (userTask): agents cannot re-route a change-set on their own.

terms.prefLabel: Triage: confirm the anchor, type and priority
terms.definition: public-comment triage / reassign / duplicate. An unplaced or low-confidence anchor is placed here, by a person.
public-comment withdraw, from any open status.

terms.prefLabel: Review the change set on its staging preview
terms.definition: The content-change review of the author's branch: its PR lists the PC refs it answers, and its staging preview is the after side of every deep link. A change the reviewers send back returns to the author inside that process.

terms.prefLabel: Edit the document as decided, on a feature branch
terms.definition: public-comment edit --branch: the author (human, or an agent in the author role) edits the folio's blocks as the decision says, on a feature branch for one change-set. Its PR says Closes #N for the change-set issue, and opening it moves that issue's accepted comments to editing. Before its preview is staged, the author writes the change set's Disposition (change set) on the Agent tab: one line per comment (No. 136: Accepted. ...), starting from each comment's Blue Disposition on Review Public Comments, after an optional Overall statement. Quality check: every comment number in the change set has a disposition; the sheet flags gaps and words that differ from the people's.

terms.prefLabel: Mark incorporated when the change set merges
terms.definition: public-comment incorporate, naming the branch, PR and staging URL; done by the folio's workflow when the PR that closes a change-set issue merges. A PR closed unmerged moves nothing. Ready for merge is set only once the QA gate has passed for the PR's head commit; set earlier, the agent does not merge until it passes. The change set's Dispositions blurb, as it stands when Ready for merge is set to Yes, is the summary that closes its issue.

terms.prefLabel: QA gate: check dispositions against the people and the pull request
terms.definition: Before Ready for merge. Reads: the change set's Disposition (change set), each comment's Blue Disposition on Review Public Comments, the PR's diff at its head commit, and the staging QA report. Checks that every comment number has one disposition; that each agrees with the people's Blue Disposition; that each Accepted or Partially accepted comment has its change in the diff, and a Not accepted, Noted, Deferred, Duplicate or Out of scope one has none; that the diff changes nothing no disposition accounts for; and that the QA report for the staged commit has no failing gate. Writes: QA gate (change set), first line "Passed <head sha>: …" or "Failed <head sha>: <why>", and QA report (change set), the report's link. The sheet shows both under Staging review; a pass for an older commit reads as stale.
Each comment that comes back through any channel is ingested and placed, triaged, grouped by theme into change sets, recommended on by the committee and decided by the editor (Process_PublicComment).

terms.prefLabel: Agree the release date and comment period
terms.definition: The review committee and the editor agree when the public comment release goes out and when comment closes. Skill: public-comment.

terms.prefLabel: Archive the release with the review
terms.definition: When comment closes, the release (PDF, PC/<version> site and the channel exports) is archived with the review record, so every comment's citation can still be followed. Run `bun run cat pc:release close`, which changes only the release's release.json; the frozen copy is never rewritten. Skill: document-publishing.

Freeze the draft as "Draft for Public Comment Release vX": a PDF with fixed line numbers and a site copy under a permanent PC/<version>/ path (not branches/, never deleted on merge). Every channel cites this release's pages, lines and block ids. Line numbers run continuously through the document. Freeze from a FULL build: dispatch the preview workflow for the branch with build_type: full first, because a preview borrows main's search index and slices; pc:release freeze refuses a preview build. Run `bun run cat pc:pdf` for the line-numbered PDF and its line map, then `bun run cat pc:release freeze` for the write-once copy under PC/<version>/. Skill: document-publishing.
The committee and the editor send the announcement through their channels. Comment is open from here until the agreed close. Skill: public-comment.

terms.prefLabel: Set up the comment channels, with instructions and links
terms.definition: Before anything is sent, the editor sets up each channel the review will use: the review sheet, the GitHub issue forms, an offline Excel sheet and a Google Form, each constrained to the release's fixed references, with precise instructions, all links, and how submitters are recorded. Skills: public-comment-channels, public-comment, review-sheet-script.

A short communication for the public: what is under review, the comment period, a high-level description of the process, and links to the release, every channel and the published process. Skills: public-comment-channels, public-comment.

terms.prefLabel: Check pages are current, links resolve
terms.definition: The generator's check mode regenerates in memory and fails on any difference from the committed pages, and on any source link that does not resolve. It runs in CI, so a change to an extraction or a library entry that was not republished fails the build rather than leaving a page that says something the extraction no longer does.

terms.prefLabel: Collect each statement with its source section
terms.definition: For every statement extracted from the library entries the artifact draws on, read three things off files: the statement verbatim, the library entry it came from, and the section of that entry, as a library reference (instance, library id, section id). The section's label is read from the entry's structure: its title and its locator in the source's own unit (a slide, a page, a cell range, a line range). For example "Catch up schedule, slide 7". A statement whose section cannot be resolved is NOT published without a link: it is reported, because a statement nobody can trace is the failure this process exists to prevent.

terms.prefLabel: Render them in the artifact's own pages
terms.definition: The statements are written into pages of the folio's working artifact, so a reader of the artifact finds them without leaving it. HOW the pages look is the content type's: its adapter renders them in its own format (pages of a document, a section of a paper, pages of an implementation guide), as its content profile declares. Each statement carries two links: to the library entry's page, and to the section, labelled as collected. The pages are GENERATED: a person edits the extraction or the source, never the page.

terms.prefLabel: Publish them in the shared viewer
terms.definition: The same statements, with the same two links, are published in the shared extraction viewer, reachable from the site's sources menu. The viewer is the cross-artifact view: every source and every statement extracted from it, whichever artifact uses them. Both places read ONE collected list, so they cannot disagree about what was extracted or where it came from.

terms.prefLabel: Read back Agentic status and Staging review
terms.definition: After the script's next run, read the row's Agentic status, Agentic status (filter) and Staging review. They must name the pull request and preview that Feedback (agent) names, and show no "no agent has picked this up" warning.

terms.prefLabel: Write the change set's Agent row
terms.definition: On the Agent tab, the change set's row: Agentic status (Not started, Working, PR open, Ready for review, Change merged or Needs human); Pull request; Staging review page; Staging built, PR head, Staging built from and Staging deploy from `agent-record.ts push`; and Agent step from `agent-record.ts step <name>`, exactly "<step> <YYYY-MM-DD HH:MMZ>" with a step from the fixed list (reading, proposing, editing, pushing, staging, deploying, qa-review, merging, proposed, idle). Prose in Agent step is not read: use idle when the row waits for people. A preview or review link is written only once it is live: the GitHub Pages deploy of a gh-pages commit at or after the preview's publish has succeeded, and an HTTP GET of each link answers 200 where the agent can reach the site. A publish that is only on the gh-pages branch is not live: Pages deploys can be queued for many minutes or cancelled by the next push. Until then Staging review page stays empty, Staging deploy says deploying, and Feedback (agent) says "Preview deploying" with no preview link.

Feedback (agent) in the fixed layout (the ask first, then Status: and Next:), linking the same pull request and preview the Agent row now names. In a log one watcher owns, another thread sends the watcher its step and links instead of writing the sheet. A preview or review link is written only once it is live: the GitHub Pages deploy of a gh-pages commit at or after the preview's publish has succeeded, and an HTTP GET of each link answers 200 where the agent can reach the site. A publish that is only on the gh-pages branch is not live: Pages deploys can be queued for many minutes or cancelled by the next push. Until then Staging review page stays empty, Staging deploy says deploying, and Feedback (agent) says "Preview deploying" with no preview link.

Runs the check again with --accept, so the state file holds what was just handled and the next poll compares against it. A row the pass could not finish stays changed and is picked up on the next poll.

terms.prefLabel: Agent pass on the changed rows
terms.definition: For each changed row, the agent pass of Contributor feedback on a working draft: Ready for agent = Yes gets its edit, Ready for merge = Yes its merge, and a Blue answer to a Decision needed question is taken up. Every new row (from an issue, a person or a TWG workbook), every row with an empty Feedback (agent) and every row whose Blue cells changed gets feedback in the same wake, in the fixed layout: the ask first (Decision needed: with lettered options, one recommended, and where to answer), then Proposed direction: and Next:, only the tags bold. The work stays inside the row's Selected Sections; a row with none gets a question asking which, and any edit outside them is named on an Outside the selected sections: line. PRs are named as repo#n, which the sheet script links, and it adds a Where to review line linking each selected section on the preview. The agent then runs tools/review-log-watch/lint.ts and fixes what it flags: a cell that breaks the layout, or a PR state that GitHub contradicts. The agent records its step on the Agent tab at once, with the real time. Previews follow main: by default (Config PREVIEW_REFRESH automatic) the agent runs tools/review-log-watch/previews.ts on every poll for every open change-set PR, and also when people act on a change set (new Blue feedback, Ready for agent set to Yes, or feedback asking to update the preview); with PREVIEW_REFRESH on-feedback, only then. A branch behind main gets main merged in (a merge commit), pushed and restaged; a conflict a person must settle is asked in the change set's feedback.

terms.prefLabel: Append rows for new issues; hide closed ones
terms.definition: For each row in the tool's append list (one per issue that no row's Issue cell links yet), appends it below the last row of Contributor Feedback: Title is the issue's title, the first Contributor Feedback column @login (#N): the issue's first paragraph, Issue its URL. The script gives each new row its Change-set id. No other writer adds issue rows. Then each row linking a closed issue (the tool's closedRows, and the rows just appended as closed) is hidden and its text struck through.

Reads Watch!F1:I1, the hash of the person-set cells that the sheet script writes on every refresh, and Contributor Feedback's header row and Issue column (a public-comment log: Review Change Sets' header row and Change-set column), and saves them as JSON for the check. A sheet without the Watch hash yet is read whole. Reading is not agent work: it changes nothing.

terms.prefLabel: Record agent step on each row it wrote
terms.definition: For every row the pass or the stall check wrote, Record agent step: the Agent tab row first (status, pull request, preview, step), then Feedback (agent) from it, then read back Agentic status and Staging review. A row whose Feedback (agent) names a pull request or preview its Agent row does not, or whose Agent step is not "<step> <time>", is fixed here.

Runs Tool review-log-watch with the folio repository, the saved values and the log's state file. The tool reads the repository's open and closed issues (no pull requests, no issue labelled no-sheet) and compares a digest of them and of the cells people set (Title, Selected Sections, Contributor Feedback, Disposition, Ready for agent, Ready for merge, Dispositions confirmed; on a public-comment log also Committee Feedback, TWG (CS), TWG (human), Change Set (human)) with the last check's. A read with no Issue column tracks only change-set issues and appends no rows, reporting them as issue-unlinked. It writes nothing.

terms.prefLabel: Hand new feedback to the row's agent; take over stalled rows
terms.definition: On every poll, changed or not, new Blue feedback goes verbatim to the agent working the row, and a stalled row is restarted or taken over. For each row: new Blue feedback goes, verbatim and in the same poll, to the thread that owns the row (named in its Agent row or Feedback (agent)), and Feedback (agent) says who has it. A row is stalled when its Blue cells changed, or Ready for agent turned Yes, more than 10 minutes ago and no Agent step was recorded since; or when its agent recorded no step for 2 hours. A stalled row's owning thread is asked once; with no answer within 10 minutes, or a thread that is done or stopped, the watcher takes the row over, or asks the coordinator for a new thread, and writes the new owner, the step and a link into Feedback (agent).
